_doc: Companion to edge_cases.json: component-keyed failure modes for infrastructure surfaces that cut across feature kinds (a payment feature can also be `queue`, a search feature can also be `cache`). Same shape: kind -> [[what, why-missed, test-that-catches-it], ...]. Loaded and merged into plan_feature.py's catalogue at runtime -- do not duplicate entries already in edge_cases.json's `realtime`, `integration`, or `payment` kinds (reconnect/backpressure/authz-per-message live in `realtime`; vendor-outage/retry-classification/secret-rotation/contract-drift live in `integration`; charge-idempotency/webhook-signature/refund live in `payment`). Combine kinds freely, e.g. `--kind payment,webhook,queue`.
cache: Cache outlives its source of truth and becomes the de facto source
the cache started as an optimization and nobody revisited that
delete the underlying row; assert the cached read eventually reflects the delete, not just the DB
Thundering herd: many concurrent misses on one key recompute in parallel
load testing never hits one key from many callers at once
expire a hot key under concurrent load; assert one recompute, not N
Stale value served indefinitely because one write path forgot to invalidate
invalidation is wired per code path, not per write
write through the code path that historically gets missed; assert the cache reflects it
Cache key omits an input that changes the value (tenant, locale, auth scope)
the key is built from the obvious params only
two tenants/users request the same nominal key; assert distinct cached values, not a leak
Negative caching absent or wrong: a miss is either re-queried every time or cached as a permanent miss
only the hit path was designed
a transient miss followed by data becoming available; assert it surfaces without waiting for TTL
Write-through cache updated before the DB transaction commits
the cache write and the DB write are not ordered against the transaction boundary
roll back the DB transaction; assert the cache was not updated ahead of it
Cached object shape drifts from a new deploy; old entries deserialize into wrong fields
cache entries are assumed to match the current code's schema
deploy a shape change with old entries still live; assert safe deserialization or a version-tagged key
Cold start or full flush causes every request to miss at once
dev never restarts the cache under load
flush the cache under production-like traffic; assert bounded recompute concurrency, not a stampede
queue: Poison message blocks the head of its queue or partition
the happy-path message always processes cleanly in dev
enqueue a message that always throws; assert it is dead-lettered, not retried forever blocking others
Visibility timeout/lease shorter than processing time causes duplicate delivery mid-processing
the timeout default is never checked against p99 processing time
process slower than the visibility timeout; assert the consumer's own idempotency prevents double effect
A dead-letter queue exists but nothing consumes or alerts on it
DLQ wiring is treated as done once the queue exists
put a message on the DLQ; assert an alert fires or an owner is paged, not silence
Consumer crashes after producing a side effect but before acknowledging
ack is assumed to follow the side effect atomically
kill the consumer between the effect and the ack; assert redelivery does not double-apply
Message exceeds the broker's size limit and is silently truncated or rejected
test messages are always small
publish a message past the size limit; assert a typed rejection at publish time, not a mangled payload downstream
Queue depth grows unbounded with no alarm or shed policy
'it will drain eventually' is the only policy
flood the queue past normal throughput; assert an alert on depth/age, not just eventual catch-up
Ordering assumed within a topic is violated once consumers scale out across partitions
single-consumer dev setup never exercises parallelism
scale consumers to 2+; assert the code only relies on per-key ordering, not topic-wide ordering
Message TTL expiry silently drops a message with no metric or log
TTL is set once for storage cost and never revisited operationally
let a message expire unconsumed; assert it is counted and visible, not just gone
cron: Two instances of the same job run concurrently after a deploy or restart overlap
a single scheduler in dev never overlaps with itself
trigger two overlapping runs; assert a lock prevents concurrent execution, not just concurrent scheduling
Job scheduled in local/server time shifts an hour at the DST boundary
the schedule is authored and tested outside DST season
freeze the scheduler clock across the DST transition; assert the run time does not silently shift
A missed run after downtime is silently skipped instead of caught up or alerted
the scheduler is always up in dev
simulate downtime spanning a scheduled run; assert either catch-up or an explicit alert, not silence
Job runtime exceeds the schedule interval, causing runs to queue or overlap indefinitely
the job is timed once on a small dataset
run the job slower than its interval; assert overlap is prevented or explicitly bounded
A job that depends on another job's output runs before that job has finished
the two schedules are authored independently with an assumed but unenforced order
delay the upstream job; assert the downstream job detects staleness rather than reading a partial result
No dead-man's-switch: nothing alerts when the job hasn't run in N expected intervals
monitoring watches the job's own success, not its absence
disable the scheduler; assert an alert fires after the missed-run threshold, not never
Supervisor silently restarts a crashed job into a half-applied state
the process manager's restart policy is set for uptime, not correctness
kill the job mid-write and let it auto-restart; assert it detects and resumes/repairs, not re-runs blindly
Cron spec timezone doesn't match the timezone the business logic assumes
the spec is written in server UTC while the feature means '9am for the customer'
assert the configured timezone matches the documented intent, with a test at a DST boundary
webhook: Receiver responds too slowly, so the sender times out and retries, creating duplicate deliveries
the handler does synchronous work before returning 2xx
make the handler slow; assert the sender's retry is absorbed by the receiver's own idempotency
A subscriber's endpoint goes stale or unreachable and failures are never surfaced to whoever configured it
delivery failure is logged on the sender's side only
point a subscription at a dead URL; assert the owner is notified, not just a log line nobody reads
Outbound delivery to a third party blocks the request that triggered it
the webhook send is written inline for simplicity
make the destination hang; assert the triggering request completes regardless
One slow or broken subscriber degrades delivery to every other subscriber in a fan-out
fan-out is implemented as a sequential loop with shared retry state
make one of three subscribers hang; assert the other two still receive their events promptly
No cap or dead-lettering on outbound retries; a permanently broken endpoint is retried forever
retry logic is copied from a case where the endpoint always eventually recovers
point at an endpoint that always fails; assert retries stop and land in a reviewable dead state
Payload shape changes with no version scheme, silently breaking subscribers
the webhook body is serialized straight from an internal model
change a field; assert existing subscribers on an old contract are not silently broken
Inbound webhook authenticated by shared secret only, no IP allowlist or mTLS option
signature verification is treated as sufficient by itself
assert the endpoint documents and, where offered, enforces a second control beyond the shared secret
Receiver logic assumes causal order the sender never promised
events usually arrive in order in manual testing
deliver two related events out of order; assert the receiver's state converges regardless of arrival order
third-party-api: 429 response ignored or handled with a blind fixed backoff instead of the vendor's Retry-After
retry logic predates this specific vendor's headers
stub a 429 with Retry-After; assert the client waits at least that long before the next attempt
Vendor SDK auto-upgrades and a minor version silently changes behavior
the SDK is a caret/range dependency, not pinned
assert the SDK version is pinned and bumped deliberately, with the changelog reviewed, not floated
Sandbox and production credentials are mixed up, sending test traffic to prod or vice versa
credentials are both just strings in the same config shape
assert environment and credential scope are checked at startup and mismatched pairs fail fast
Pagination cursor expires mid-crawl of a large result set
test datasets are small enough to finish inside the cursor's TTL
stub a cursor expiry partway through a paged crawl; assert a typed recoverable error, not silent data loss
A batch/bulk API call's partial success (some items succeed, some fail) is reported as all-or-nothing
the response is checked for a single top-level status
stub a batch response with mixed per-item results; assert each item's outcome is handled individually
Vendor timestamp format or timezone assumed but never verified (epoch vs ISO8601, UTC vs local)
the field parses fine in the timezone the developer is sitting in
feed a non-UTC or non-ISO timestamp from the vendor's documented format; assert correct interpretation
API deprecation/sunset notice ignored until the cutover date arrives in production
sunset headers or changelogs are not monitored
assert there is a named owner and a check that surfaces a Sunset/Deprecation header before it fires in prod
Vendor status page says operational while the specific endpoint in use is actually degraded
the status page's granularity is coarser than the integration's dependency
stub a degraded response while asserting the app does not rely on the status page as its own health signal
multi-tenancy: A query missing a tenant/org filter returns or mutates another tenant's rows
the happy path is tested with one tenant in the database
seed two tenants; assert every list/read/write is scoped, not just the one used in manual testing
Cache or queue keys collide across tenants because the id wasn't namespaced
the key was built before multi-tenancy existed and never revisited
two tenants with the same nominal id/key; assert no cross-tenant value returned or consumed
One tenant's load starves another's on shared infrastructure with no per-tenant quota
load testing only ever exercises a single tenant
drive one tenant to its limit; assert another tenant's latency/throughput is unaffected
Tenant offboarding leaves orphaned data in secondary stores (search index, cache, queue, blob storage)
deletion is implemented against the primary database only
delete a tenant; assert search, cache, and blob storage no longer reference it, not just the DB row
A background job iterating 'all tenants' aborts the whole batch on one tenant's failure
the loop has no per-tenant error boundary
make one tenant's iteration throw; assert every other tenant still completes
A plan-tier or feature-flag check is bypassable via a client-controlled parameter
the check reads a field the client can also set
attempt to set the gated field directly; assert server-side enforcement independent of client input
A migration or backfill script runs without a tenant filter, touching tenants not ready for the change
the script was written for a single-tenant mental model
assert scripts that mutate data accept and default to an explicit tenant scope, not 'all rows'
Tenant-specific configuration (timezone, currency, locale) silently defaults to another tenant's setting
config defaults are global constants, not per-tenant lookups
two tenants with different locale settings; assert output honors each tenant's own configuration
pii-compliance: PII logged in plaintext in application or access logs
logging is added for debugging without a redaction pass
grep captured logs for email/phone/name patterns after a normal request flow; assert none appear
PII embedded in an error message returned to the client or sent to an error tracker
the exception message interpolates the input that caused it
trigger a validation error on a PII field; assert the response and the error-tracking payload are scrubbed
Deleted user's PII persists past the stated retention policy in backups, caches, search indexes, or queued payloads
deletion is implemented against the primary table only
delete a user; assert PII is gone or scheduled-for-purge in every store it reached, not just the DB row
A subject-access-request export reads the primary DB only, missing PII replicated to analytics/warehouse/cache
the export query was written before the data had secondary homes
request an export; assert it covers every store PII has flowed into, per the recorded data map
PII sent to a third party (analytics, support tool, LLM API) with no documented legal basis or DPA
the integration was added for a feature need, not reviewed for data flow
assert every third-party destination of PII has a recorded legal basis, in the decision log
Access to PII fields is unscoped and unaudited — any authenticated caller can read the column
the field is just another column on an authorized model
assert a role without explicit PII access is denied, and that access is logged
PII used as a natural key (e.g. email as primary key) blocks honoring a deletion/right-to-be-forgotten request without breaking referential integrity
the key was chosen for convenience, not for the ability to purge it later
assert PII fields are not depended on as immutable identifiers elsewhere in the schema
Masking is applied only at the display layer while the API response still carries the unmasked value
redaction is a UI-layer concern in the code as written
call the API directly, bypassing the UI; assert PII is masked in the payload itself, not just on screen
batch-job: Job is not idempotent: a rerun after partial failure double-applies already-processed rows
the job is designed for a single clean run
kill the job partway through and rerun it; assert no row is double-charged/double-sent/double-counted
No checkpoint or resume; a job killed near the end restarts from zero
checkpointing is added only if someone asks for it
kill the job at 90% completion; assert it resumes near there, not from the start
Job holds a long transaction or lock on a production-sized table, blocking normal traffic
it was only ever tested against a small dev table
measure lock duration against a realistic row count; assert it stays under an explicit bound or chunks its work
Concurrent runs of the same job race on the same rows (overlapping schedule plus a manual trigger)
the job is assumed to run alone
start two runs at once; assert a lock or claim mechanism prevents double-processing
Job logs 'completed' even though a subset of rows failed silently
success is reported at the job level, not per row
make a subset of rows fail; assert the job's reported status reflects partial failure, not blanket success
Memory grows unbounded because the job loads the full dataset instead of streaming or paginating
dev datasets fit comfortably in memory
run against a dataset larger than available memory; assert bounded memory via streaming/paging
No dry-run mode for a job that mutates data, so the first real run is also the first tested run
dry-run is skipped to save time under deadline
assert a dry-run flag exists and its output was reviewed before the first real execution
A downstream consumer reads the job's output before its commit/flush completes
the job's own completion signal fires before data is durably visible
race a downstream read against the job's tail end; assert the consumer only sees fully committed output
file-storage: A bucket or object defaults to public when it should be private
the storage provider's default ACL is assumed to be safe
assert new buckets/objects are private by default and public access requires an explicit, reviewed decision
A presigned URL has no expiry, or one long enough to be effectively permanent
the expiry parameter is copied from an example and never revisited
generate a presigned URL; assert it stops working after its stated, short expiry
Large upload/download is not resumable or streamed; a dropped connection restarts from zero
test files are small enough to finish in one request
drop the connection mid-transfer on a large file; assert resume rather than a full restart
Two uploads deriving the same key silently overwrite each other
keys are derived from user-supplied names without a uniqueness guarantee
upload two different files that derive the same key; assert a collision is detected, not a silent overwrite
A deleted file's references elsewhere (DB rows, search index, cached URLs) are not cleaned up
deletion is implemented against storage only
delete an object; assert every referencing record is updated or the reference is treated as stale, not broken
A lifecycle/storage-class policy archives or deletes a file a live feature still depends on
the lifecycle rule was written by an infra team without a feature-owner review
assert lifecycle rules are cross-checked against active feature dependencies before applying to a prefix
Cross-region replication lag causes a just-uploaded file to 404 when read from another region immediately after write
single-region dev never exercises replication
write then immediately read from a different region; assert the read path tolerates or waits out replication lag
No integrity check after upload; a corrupted transfer is stored and served as if valid
a successful HTTP status is treated as proof of a correct transfer
corrupt a small percentage of bytes in transit in a test harness; assert a checksum mismatch is caught, not served
notification: Duplicate notification sent because marking-as-sent and sending are not atomic
a crash between the send and the record-of-send causes a retry to resend
kill the process between send and record; assert redelivery does not send a second copy
A user's opt-out/unsubscribe preference is not checked before send
the send path was built before preferences existed and was never wired to check them
opt a user out; assert no further notification of that type reaches them
Notification is queued but the provider silently rejects it, and nothing surfaces the rejection
success is assumed once the provider API call returns 2xx at enqueue time
stub a provider rejection after acceptance; assert it is surfaced to an owner, not just dropped
Bounce/complaint feedback from the provider is not fed back to suppress future sends to a bad address
feedback webhooks from the provider were never wired up
simulate a bounce webhook; assert the address is suppressed for future sends
A templated batch send leaks one recipient's data into another recipient's message via a shared template context
the template is rendered once and reused across a loop without a fresh context per recipient
send to two recipients with different data in one batch; assert no cross-recipient leakage in either message
Provider rate limit hit mid-bulk-send and the remaining batch fails without retry or backoff
bulk send is a tight loop with no throttling
drive a bulk send past the provider's rate limit; assert the remainder is retried/throttled, not dropped
An invalid or expired push token (uninstalled app) errors accumulate instead of being pruned
token invalidation feedback from the push provider is not consumed
simulate an invalid-token response; assert the token is removed rather than retried indefinitely
A scheduled notification is timezone-naive and arrives at 3am local for the recipient
the schedule is computed in the server's timezone
schedule for a recipient in a different timezone than the server; assert delivery lands in their local daytime window as specified
